lead.title: OpenAI trims funding round target from ~$30B to $20B as investors cool
lead.summary: OpenAI has cut its fundraising target from $30B at a $1.25T valuation to roughly $20B, with ~$11B secured so far and a UAE-led group expected to lead, per FT and WSJ reporting. A follow-up retail offering for wealthy individuals could complete the target — the latest sign that capital is shifting from hype toward revenue and cash flow.

top_stories.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to ~60,000 employees amid AI capex
top_stories.summary: Roughly a quarter of Microsoft's workforce in the US, UK, Canada and India is eligible for voluntary exit packages as the company reins in costs while funding AI and datacenter spending. Uptake is expected in the low thousands rather than a forced mass layoff.

top_stories.title: NVIDIA dials back Rubin GPU specs as first production hardware ships
top_stories.summary: HBM4 memory bandwidth and NVLink bandwidth are down versus earlier targets, with FP4 training cut from 280 to 270 PFLOPS and FP8 from 140 to 130 PFLOPS. The changes apply to HGX Rubin NVL8, Vera Rubin NVL8 and DGX systems, though network bandwidth per system rises from 1.6 to 1.8 TB/s.

top_stories.title: Intel shifts wafer capacity from consumer to server CPUs amid 'unprecedented' AI demand
top_stories.summary: Intel is expanding Fab 24 in Ireland and converting Oregon 18A capacity meant for Panther Lake into Intel 3 for more Xeons. DCAI revenue hit $7.3B in Q3, up nearly 80% year over year, and Intel warns supply constraints will stay severe through H1 2027.

top_stories.title: Zero-mean activation 'bug' linked to LLM loss spikes, backed by Yann LeCun
top_stories.summary: Ziming Liu (Tsinghua, KAN researcher) showed that common activations (ReLU, SiLU/GeLU) have non-zero mean post-activation output, causing ill-conditioned training dynamics — loss spikes and representation overshoot in LLMs and ViTs — with measurable gains from fixing it. LeCun replied in agreement, noting the effect has been understood since a 1990 NeurIPS paper.

items.title: Observation-anchored latent diffusion recovers missing triples in knowledge graphs
items.summary: Triple set prediction is reframed from recovering isolated links to predicting whole triple sets, replacing the dominant subgraph-completion paradigm with an observation-anchored latent diffusion approach that unifies local recovery with global generation.

items.title: Escaping path mirages in offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning
items.summary: In stochastic long-horizon settings, compounding value-estimation errors create 'path mirages' that derail goal reaching. The paper characterizes the failure mode and proposes a method that reliably navigates it.

items.title: The value of information: one quantity for retrieval and credit assignment
items.summary: For memory-equipped agents, both cheap retrieval (finding the relevant item without scoring the whole store) and credit assignment (rewarding the act of acquiring a memory) are argued to be governed by a single quantity — the value of information.

items.title: Learning calibrated confidence for multi-agent collaboration
items.summary: In multi-hop, multi-agent information seeking, upstream agents produce intermediate answers downstream agents must trust. The work trains specialized agents to emit calibrated confidence signals, improving evidence collection across documents.

items.title: Safe multi-objective RL with zero constraint violation and primal-averaging convergence
items.summary: A framework for policies that balance conflicting objectives while satisfying cumulative and stepwise safety constraints throughout learning — not just at convergence — with primal-averaging convergence guarantees.

items.title: Read, allocate, route: role-coupled tokenization for pixel-space generative transformers
items.summary: Not all image patches need equal treatment: low-frequency structure benefits from global tokens while fine detail can be handled locally. Role-coupled tokenization routes information by role, cutting the cost of global attention as resolution grows.

items.title: One vector or many? Clustered optimal-transport steering under quantization
items.summary: Activation steering usually adds a single difference-of-class-means vector to hidden states. CHaRS instead uses concept-heterogeneity-aware optimal transport, and the paper compares the two under quantization.

items.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: one encoder, one schema, all modalities
items.summary: An omni-modal parser that converts documents, images, audio and video into structured records grounded in space and time, providing the perception layer for agents that read, locate and cite evidence across modalities.

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources a research coding agent that turns GitHub requests into PRs
items.summary: DeepSeek's Harness team open-sourced a research-prototype coding agent that accepts authorized GitHub requests and returns pull requests — an open alternative in the agent space. Separate reports show DeepSeek v4.1 Flash running on 64 GB RAM via heavy quantization and disk paging.

items.title: Flint (Recursive): new open 2.5B-active coding model claims 74% on SWE-bench Verified
items.summary: Recursive's Flint is a new open coding model with 2.5B active parameters claiming 74% on SWE-bench Verified — already trending on Hugging Face (RecursiveSI/flint, unsloth/flint-GGUF).

items.title: Pika launches H3 Flex, an open-weight video-and-audio generation model
items.summary: Pika released H3 Flex, an open-weight model generating video with independently editable audio tracks — extending open weights into joint video+audio generation.

items.title: Qwen's wild side: 'nesformer' runs a NES emulator inside Qwen3.5-4B weights
items.summary: Community experimentation around Qwen peaks: 'Qwenputer' runs an LLM inside Qwen3.5-4B weights using their layers as RAM, and 'nesformer' plays Super Mario from a 6502 emulator compiled into the weights. Small uncensored 4B GGUFs are also circulating, with Qwen4 and 1M context heavily anticipated.

items.title: Prospero: a coding harness for local open-weight LLMs
items.summary: A coding harness optimized for local open-weight models, letting them handle programming tasks reliably on consumer hardware.

items.title: Karpathy launches HackerTube, a YouTube built from HN recommendations
items.summary: A video platform curated by Andrej Karpathy that aggregates YouTube videos recommended by Hacker News users.

items.title: Framer ships AI agents on the design canvas
items.summary: A major update lets designers use AI agents directly on the canvas to design, write, analyze and publish professional sites.

items.title: Floot builds and publishes real apps without leaving ChatGPT
items.summary: A tool to build and publish real apps entirely inside ChatGPT, launching on Product Hunt.

items.title: Radar: open-source site reliability engineering insights for AI agents
items.summary: An open-source tool that provides SRE-style observability and insights for AI agents, launched on Product Hunt.
